headline: Site walk at 24 Worthley Road discussed steep driveway grades and possible blasting for a two-lot subdivision.
summary: Walkers checked the steep access easement, where the grade reaches as much as 14.8%. A resident worried that blasting to build the grade could damage her well. A shared driveway with the Nottonsons' driveway was suggested, which would need a waiver, and the hearing continues November 04, 2026.
decisions: Continued the public hearing on the 2 lot subdivision to November 04, 2026.

transcript:
# Derry Planning Board

## Site Walk Notes

Saturday, October 17, 2026

Proposal: 2 Lot Subdivision

PID/Location: 12006, 24 Worthley Road

Owner: Nottonson Family Revocable Trust

*Objective: to examine existing conditions and to gain a better understanding of proposed conditions relative to the 2-lot subdivision. The Planning Board opened the public hearing for this proposal on October 07, 2026, and continued it to November 04, 2026.*

Planning Board Members Present: David Nelson, Richard Malaby, Brian Chirichiello, Michael Wood, Derek Minervini, Thomas Mauzy, Z. Michael Appleton, Andrew Young (Absent: John O'Connor, Randy Chase, Bryan Fishman, Jacob Pelletier)

Members of the Public Present at Various Times: Karen Nottonson, Brian Corliss, Janet Corliss, Paul Dionne, Susan Dionne, Neil Wetherbee

Planning Department Staff Present: Caroline Wilson

The site walk began at 1:09pm at the "turnabout" area located before the driveway for the existing dwelling at 24 Worthley. Conditions were clear, dry, and ~45-50 degrees Fahrenheit.

Iron pins set by Promised Land Survey marking the proposed frontage of the new lot were observed and acknowledged to be approximately 72' apart. It was noted that utility easement(s) exist, some utility poles were marked with blue tape.

The group traversed the access easement uphill towards the Corliss residence. The grade reaches as much as 14.8% (note: the LDCR allows a maximum of 15%). Ms. Dionne believed that blasting would have to be done in order to produce the proposed grade; and she was concerned such blasting could damage her well.

It was Ms. Nottonson's understanding from the surveyor, Neal McCarthy (not present), that the location of the driveway, dwelling, septic, etc., could be amended.

The group headed back down the hill and walked in the direction of the Nottonsons' driveway. It was suggested that a portion of the Nottonsons' driveway could be shared with the new dwelling's driveway to avoid utilizing the steep access easement. (This would require a waiver - the Board does not always support shared driveways).

The site walk will be discussed at the continuation of the public hearing for the subdivision, on Wednesday, November 04, 2026.

The site walk concluded at 1:45pm.

The notes were prepared by Caroline Wilson.

Approved by: [signature]

Chairman/Vice ~~Chairman~~

[signature]

Secretary PRO TEM

Approval date: November 04, 2026
